8 commits churn (reason plumbing, atomic Change Notes append, [DISCARDED] decoration)

clean src; no inline debt markers

findings.claim: diagnoseHealth (IR-CLI-051 env-health doctor) is exported but imported nowhere in src/; `speckiwi doctor` CLI wires runPackageDoctor (OPS-NODE-003) instead. IR-CLI-051 returns NOT_FOUND via MCP get_requirement and appears only in v3.0.0 plan/.kiwi artifacts — stranded, uncommitted v3.0.0 WIP.
findings.suggested_tool_or_feature: v3.0.0 must reconcile the two doctors: wire diagnoseHealth as `speckiwi doctor` (with --fix), rename package smoke to `speckiwi doctor package`/release-smoke or merge; remove/register dangling @req IR-CLI-051.

findings.claim: Two CLI tests drive the SAME `speckiwi doctor --json` with mutually exclusive contracts: doctor.ir-cli-051.test asserts checks[].state in {ok,warn,fail}+health topics; doctor-command.test asserts checks[].status in {pass,fail,warn,skip}+package/mcp shape. vitest.config has no test exclude so both run — one is a failing/landmine test.
findings.suggested_tool_or_feature: Delete/quarantine the superseded doctor test and settle a single `speckiwi doctor` contract before v3.0.0 wiring.

findings.claim: Three distinct 'doctor' concepts share the word with divergent state vocabularies and two same-named-but-different DoctorCheck interfaces: `speckiwi doctor` (package smoke, status pass/fail/warn/skip), `speckiwi workflow doctor` (artifact projection, outcomeCodes/blocking), unwired env-health (state ok/warn/fail).
findings.suggested_tool_or_feature: Unify doctor taxonomy (`speckiwi doctor --scope env|package|workflow` or `doctor --all`) and a shared HealthCheck type.

findings.claim: --input-json/--help --json (IR-CLI-043) is limited to 22 MUTATION commands; read commands (list,summary,search,validate) and the ~25 `workflow *` subcommands (many with path/runId/target/limit/offset) do NOT accept a single JSON payload, forcing positional/flag encoding for programmatic agents.
findings.suggested_tool_or_feature: Extend the input-json/help-json expander to read + workflow commands so every command accepts one JSON object.

findings.claim: input-json.ts documents an internal SSOT drift (FND-001): ToolSpec.args is empty for CLI-only commands and disagrees with CLI positionals, so positionals must be re-sourced from commander registeredArguments; the registry carries no positional-arg metadata.
findings.suggested_tool_or_feature: Make ToolSpec carry positional args (single SSOT for CLI+MCP+help) to remove the registeredArguments workaround.

findings.claim: Requirement-ID collision repair handles ONE duplicateId per plan/apply; diagnose surfaces all groups and apply returns pendingDuplicateGroups, but multi-collision merges need N manual diagnose->plan->apply cycles. No batch/plan-all surface.
findings.suggested_tool_or_feature: `repair requirement-id-collisions plan-all` producing a multi-group plan (explicit keep/rename per group) + apply-all iterating with per-group evidence.

findings.claim: workflow/read.ts hardcodes SRS diagnostic codes (SRS-W050..W069/E032/E074) across >=3 classifier switches (outcomeCodesFromDiagnostics, diffClassFor, projectionBlocking); adding one code needs edits in multiple functions -> drift risk.
findings.suggested_tool_or_feature: Single diagnostic-code registry table mapping code->{class,outcomeCode,blocking}, reused by all projections (mirror src/core/diagnostic-registry.ts).

findings.claim: src/mcp/server.ts is a ~540-line monolith holding all zod input schemas plus tool-name arrays for ~60 tools; it is the #1 src churn file (8 commits) and a merge-conflict hotspot.
findings.suggested_tool_or_feature: Colocate each tool's zod schema with its registration (or split by domain) so adding a tool touches one place.

findings.claim: vitest coverage.include omits src/core/health/** and src/doctor/**, so both doctor modules carry no coverage threshold — env-health and package-smoke diagnostics are unmeasured.
findings.suggested_tool_or_feature: Add src/core/health and src/doctor to coverage include, or fold health into a covered path.

findings.claim: Of 72 v2.3.0 requirements, countsByStability is 71 evolving / 1 stable; the 'tool improvement' release verified behavior but almost nothing reached stable/frozen change-control maturity.
findings.suggested_tool_or_feature: A target-wide stability promotion gate (kiwi-srs-feasibility / `speckiwi stabilize`) to move verified REQs to stable before v3.0.0 opens edits.

findings.claim: No CLI/MCP surface to inspect or release a stale SRS mutation lock; agents can only pass --ignore-lock on apply. A crashed owner's lock relies on implicit TTL/owner-safe recovery with no `lock status`/`lock release` command.
findings.suggested_tool_or_feature: `speckiwi lock status|release` (+MCP) to view holder/TTL and force-release with reason instead of blanket --ignore-lock.

findings.claim: docs/analysis contains bulk requirement-registration scripts (register-netnew.mjs, register-p0p1.mjs, register-p2p3.mjs, register-part3.mjs, fix-priority.mjs). Their existence implies add_requirement is one-at-a-time with no first-class batch/bulk-import tool, so agents wrote ad-hoc drivers.
findings.evidence_path: git-status untracked: docs/analysis/register-p0p1.mjs, register-p2p3.mjs, register-netnew.mjs, register-part3.mjs, fix-priority.mjs
findings.suggested_tool_or_feature: A guarded batch `add_requirements` (array input, dry-run plan, per-item validation) to replace hand-written .mjs registration scripts.

findings.claim: Large uncommitted working tree on feat/2.3 (src impl + docs) with paused v3.0.0 pipeline WIP (16/206) intermixed; there is no tool to verify each SRS-verified REQ's @req tag exists in TRACKED source, so shipped-vs-WIP is ambiguous.
findings.evidence_path: git-status: many src/core/mutation/*.ts, src/core/health/, src/cli/input-json.ts untracked; .kiwi/sessions/2026-06-17.speckiwi.v3-0-0/*
findings.suggested_tool_or_feature: An SRS<->tracked-code trace check (extend doctor): flag verified REQs whose @req tag is only in untracked/uncommitted files.

findings.claim: kiwi/pipeline.jsonl SSOT is NOT double-parsed by skills alone — v2.3.0 shipped a full CLI+MCP workflow surface reading it (pipeline-status/tail/next/compact, session-status, resume-hint, worklog-tail, doctor/diff/schema-check) with CLI/MCP parity. Focus-Q4 gap is largely closed.
findings.suggested_tool_or_feature: No new tool needed; remaining gap is that skills should PREFER these readers over raw-file parsing (partly in MIG-FLOW-003/004).
